title: Investigatio motuum, quibus laminae et virgae elasticae contremiscunt

deep.reconstruction:
Context: E526 treats the transverse vibrations of an elastic rod (Euler–Bernoulli beam equation). In this section one end, E (u=0, s=0), is free and the other end (u=1, s=a) is simply supported (pinned). Normalise abscissa u=s/a. The spatial mode found on the previous page is
y(u) = e^{uω} − e^{ω(2−u)} + (1+e^{2ω}) sin uω + (1−e^{2ω}) cos uω.
This page rewrites it, dropping the time-dependent factor, as
y = (e^{uω}+sin uω+cos uω) − e^{2ω}(e^{−uω} − sin uω + cos uω).
This form satisfies y''(0)=y'''(0)=0, the free-end conditions. Setting y(1)=0 gives tan ω = tanh ω. Since tanh ω≈1, the fundamental root is approximately ω=5π/4; the exact value is 3.92660, i.e. 5π/4 − 0.0004. Then e^{2ω}=e^{5π/2}≈2576.
Euler tabulates the fundamental mode shape at u = 0, 1/5, 2/5, 3/5, 4/5, 1 so that it can be drawn (Fig. 7):
(I) u=0: y = 2 − 2e^{2ω} = −5150, the deflection of the free end E.
(II) u=1/5: here uω=π/4, e^{π/4}=2.1933 and e^{−π/4}=0.4559. The first bracket is 2.1933+√2 = 3.6075. In the second bracket the sine and cosine cancel, leaving 0.4559. Hence y = 3.6075 − 2576·0.4559 ≈ −1171.
(III) u=2/5: the computation is set up and continues on the next page.
The purpose is to exhibit the fundamental free–pinned mode shape and to locate its single node. On the following page this leads to the inference that the k-th mode has k nodes.
errors: Minor and harmless: using the approximate root ω=5π/4 instead of the exact 3.92660 means y(1) is −√2 rather than 0. This is negligible relative to values of order 10^3.
Not on this page, but on the next page the transcription shows y(2/5)=0.2079; the correct value is about 2046. The printed y(3/5)=3387 should be about 3409.

ideas.what: Mode shape of a free–pinned Euler–Bernoulli beam, written as a combination of exponentials and trigonometric functions, with frequency equation tan ω = tanh ω
ideas.modern_name: Free–pinned (free–hinged) beam eigenfunction; characteristic equation tan βL = tanh βL
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler and Daniel Bernoulli (1735–1744 beam vibration work); E526 for the full catalogue of end conditions; later Rayleigh for the systematic treatment
ideas.where_published: E526 (Acta Acad. Sci. Petrop. 1779, publ. 1782); cf. E65 Additamentum De curvis elasticis (1744) for earlier cases

ideas.what: Numerical tabulation of the fundamental mode shape at fifths of the length to draw the figure and locate the node
ideas.modern_name: Numerical evaluation and plotting of an eigenfunction / nodal location

ideas.what: Approximation of the root of tan ω = tanh ω by 5π/4, because tanh ω ≈ 1

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine numerical evaluation of a known mode shape from a well-studied paper (Truesdell's account of rational elasticity covers E526). The arithmetic is correct and nothing new is introduced.
transcription_corrections: The leading '1(' in 'y = 1(e^{uω}…' is just the opening bracket with a possible stray mark; read 'y = (e^{uω}+sin uω+cos uω) − e^{2ω}(…)'.
'−1171' is printed as '−1171.' in the image. The figure looks like '−117I' but should be read as −1171.
